misclassified_entities.reason: Internal to the EIP governance process - EIP editors are part of the Ethereum specification governance system, not external entities sending data into the system
Governance entity - Origin providers interact with the EIP editorial process, not with runtime Ethereum execution

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human operator with physical/administrative access to validator. Authenticated via system access but slashing protection data must still be fully validated to prevent accidental or malicious corruption.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Consensus layer node authenticated typically via JWT. Requests block/attestation signatures. Must validate all signing requests against slashing rules even from authenticated beacon node.

trusted_external_entities.name: Previous Validator Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Interchange file from another validator client. Could be maliciously crafted to allow slashable signing by omitting records. Full schema and semantic validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Trace Consumer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External debugging tool consuming trace output. Typically used in controlled testing environments. Output only - no input validation concern, but access control needed.

trusted_external_entities.name: Trace Requester
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External entity requesting transaction tracing - explicitly identified as potential DoS vector. Tracing is expensive and should be rate-limited and access-controlled.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Community Member
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any community member can propose origin additions. Proposals must go through full EIP editor review process. No direct system access.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying Ethereum state via JSON-RPC. Network peer with no inherent authentication. All query parameters must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or application submitting EIP-1559 type-2 transactions. All transaction fields must be validated including fee parameters, signature, and balance requirements.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator producing blocks. Authenticated via consensus mechanism but blocks must still pass all EIP-1559 validation rules including gas limit bounds and base fee calculation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Validator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator receiving priority fees. Part of consensus but priority fee distribution follows deterministic rules - no trust in validator honesty for fee calculation.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Validator must be completely stopped during import. File must pass JSON schema validation, genesis root check, and BLS pubkey validation. Missing signing roots treated as conflicts.
Even from authenticated beacon node, must check block slot against slashing database. Never sign block at slot below minimum. Never sign conflicting block at same slot.
Must check for surround voting. Source and target epochs must be at or above minimum previously signed. Never sign attestation that would be slashable.
Full validation pipeline required: JSON schema, BLS pubkey format, signing root format. Conservative handling of missing signing roots. Could be maliciously crafted.
Tracing must be explicitly enabled via config flag. DoS risk from expensive computation. Should only be exposed on debug/test nodes, never public RPC endpoints.
Proposals enter governance review process. Must pass unique identification, 10-year availability history, and free access requirements before approval.
Block parameter format must be validated. Object format must not have both blockNumber and blockHash. requireCanonical flag must be respected. Proper error codes for missing/non-canonical blocks.
Full transaction validation: EIP-2718 type-2 format, max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee, sender balance >= (gas_limit * max_fee) + value. Signature verification required.

coverage_gaps.reason: Output-only entity - receives trace data but does not send data into the system. No incoming trust boundary edge.
Receives priority fees as output. Fee distribution is deterministic based on transaction execution, not an incoming data flow.
